question: Which of the following numbers is a perfect square?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the **unit digit** of the given numbers. A **perfect square** never ends in 2, 3, 7, or 8.

Option 1 (222) ends in 2 → **Not a perfect square**.

Check known squares of numbers near 10 and 15: 10² = 100, 14² = 196, 15² = 225.

We see that 14 × 14 = 196.

**∴ The correct answer is 196.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A list of numbers to identify a **perfect square**.

**Formula:** A number **n** is a perfect square if √n is an **integer**.

⇒ √222 ≈ 14.89 (Not an integer)

⇒ √124 ≈ 11.13 (Not an integer)

⇒ √141 ≈ 11.87 (Not an integer)

⇒ √196 = 14 (Integer)

Since 14² = 14 × 14 = 196, it is a perfect square.

**∴ The correct answer is 196.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Digit Rule

The last digit of a **perfect square** must be 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9. It can never be 2, 3, 7, or 8.

Digital Sum Property

The **digital sum** (sum of digits until a single digit is reached) of a perfect square is always 1, 4, 7, or 9.

Common Squares

11² = 121, 12² = 144, 13² = 169, 14² = 196, 15² = 225.</p
